note: How the scenario moves a rating. Read by src/lib/score.js. Every rule here fires on data the tool already holds: the fetched weapon stats, the game own tags, or fields curated in items.json. Nothing here is a hand written per item list. A rule states a delta in points, where roughly 14 points is one tier, or scales one from a number the game publishes. Every rule must carry a `say`, because a score that cannot explain itself is a score nobody should trust. And every rule must fire on something that actually varies with the scenario, which is the test the armour rules failed.
whyThereAreNoArmourRules: There were five, added in 1.10.0 and removed in 1.13.0, and they were the wrong altitude. Measured on the Automaton front, 48 of 51 primaries shared one of two identical armour readings and 42 of them lost a tier for it. A rule that fires the same way on 94% of a population is not telling you anything about any of them. The deeper error: a community tier already prices in what an item is for. Voters know an assault rifle does not open a Hulk, so the Liberator's B on bots is a B given that it is a chaff gun, and penalising it again charges twice for one fact. The test to apply to any replacement is whether the thing it fires on actually varies with the scenario. Armour reach per item does not; it is constant, and only the front and difficulty move it, which moves every primary together. That makes it a loadout property. src/lib/squad.js already had this right, asking whether anyone in the squad carries AP 4 or better rather than judging each weapon alone, and that is the shape armour scoring should come back in.
sourceOfHazardWording: The hazard mechanics quoted in these sentences come from the helldivers-2/json community dataset, MIT licensed. They are the game's own descriptions, not our guesses.

rules.say: Icy temperatures delay heat buildup, so this fires longer before it vents. The game publishes the figure per weapon and this one is above average.
High temperatures speed up heat buildup, so this overheats sooner than it does anywhere else.
Cold reduces rate of fire, and a weapon that leans on a high rate of fire feels that more than a slow one does.
Ion storms intermittently disable Stratagems. Anything you have to call in can simply not arrive.
Ion storms cannot switch off what is already in your hands, which is worth more here than it usually is.

Sandstorms greatly reduce visibility while they last, and range stops being an advantage. They are weather rather than climate though: roughly three minutes at a time, so this is a risk you carry rather than a state you are in.

rules.say: Tremors stun players and enemies alike, and this cannot be reloaded on the move. Being stunned mid reload is how a fight gets away from you.
Tremors stun anything standing on the ground, including you while you are setting this up.
The planet is already on fire. Adding to it makes telling your fire from the planet's harder, and fire resist armor is doing double duty.
Acid storms temporarily reduce armor effectiveness for everyone, so a passive that leans on staying alive through damage is worth a little less.
Terminids are mostly large fleshy parts, and durable damage is what hurts those. This one keeps most of its damage against them where a chaff gun loses it.
Almost all of this weapon's damage is standard rather than durable, which a Charger's backside and a Spewer's sack largely ignore.
Poor ergonomics means the barrel lags behind the camera, and Hunters do not wait for you to catch up.
The Crusher regenerates while taking heavy damage and has to be worn down without a pause. A deep magazine is how you get one.
Reloading between shots gives a Crusher the pause it needs to regenerate. Burst damage is worth less on this front than it looks.
Demolition 40 closes a hole or a fabricator from outside, without spending a call-in. On this mission that is the whole job.
Closes objectives from your carried kit rather than by burning a stratagem, which is what this mission asks for over and over.
Carrying the objective means this is on your back, not in your hands, for most of the walk.
Smoke breaks the line of sight along the route the civilians have to walk, which is the whole problem this mission sets.
One arena and no ground to give up. Anything you can plant and leave finally gets to sit still long enough to pay for itself.
A set number of named heavies and nothing else counts, so opening heavy armor is the entire loadout question.
Twelve minutes and a map full of structures. Closing one from outside, without lining up a throw, is what the clock rewards.

You will have an objective in one hand for most of this mission. A one handed weapon lets you shoot while carrying it; everything else means putting it down first. It does not make a bad sidearm good, it makes a good one indispensable.

Under this much pressure on a bot planet, the fight you win is the one you do not start. A suppressed weapon is audible at 12 metres rather than 100, so a sentry on a perimeter dies without waking the base behind it. This is the difference between walking through an outpost and running from it.
rules.source: The five suppressed weapons, and this is sourced rather than judged: the wiki carries Suppressed as a trait in each weapon's infobox and states that a suppressed weapon has an audible range of 12 metres against 100 for everything else. Listed by id here because the fetch does not read weapon article infoboxes yet. Move it into the fetch when it does.
rules.judgement: Ours. The size is set by one choice: being unheard is worth about a tier at peril 22, which is solo on Impossible or a duo on Helldive. Everything else follows from the scale. Below zero it inverts on purpose: with four of you on Challenging a silenced weapon is effort spent on a problem you do not have.
rules.sayInverted: There is enough slack in this drop that nothing needs to be a secret. Staying unheard costs you rate of fire and stopping power, and at this level you are not being punished for making noise. Bring the louder gun.

rules.say: Every shot from this brings the patrol, and at this level there is not enough slack to absorb one more fight. On paper it may be the better gun. Here the noise is the stat that decides the run.
rules.judgement: Ours, and deliberately gentler than the reward it mirrors. This matches almost half of everything you can hold, so it is set at roughly three quarters of a tier at peril 22 rather than a full one. A rule that touches half a list has to argue quietly.
rules.sayInverted: Loud is free here. Whatever the noise brings, this drop has the slack to hold it, and at this level it does not bring much. This is the situation the community rating already assumes, so nothing about it counts against this.

rules.say: A storm cuts their sight as much as yours, and under this much pressure you are not trying to win the firefight. Reduced visibility plus a weapon nobody hears is the difference between crossing an outpost and being chased out of one.
rules.judgement: Ours. Stacks with the plain quiet rule rather than replacing it, so a storm is worth extra on top rather than instead. Sized at about six tenths of a tier at peril 22.
rules.sayInverted: A storm cuts your sight as much as theirs, and this drop is comfortable enough that the fight is one you can simply win. Trading reach for silence is the wrong trade here.

knownGaps: Three visibility rules lean on a long-range tag that is our judgement rather than a published field. It lives in vocabulary.json with its reasoning, and the rules that read it carry a `judgement` saying so. It used to be the same six ids written out inside each of those three rules.

The visibility rules key on the Marksman category only. Special was tried and dropped: it holds a flamethrower, a stim pistol and a shotgun pistol alongside the Dominator, so it says nothing about range.

Armour penetration moves no rating at the item level and it must not. It moves one at the loadout level as of 1.20.0: build-rules.json reads the best thing a build holds against the front, which splits the 39 curated builds 36 / 41 / 23 where the per item reading split 51 primaries 48 to 3. Enemy armour is still shown on every expanded row as a fact. See whyThereAreNoArmourRules, which is about this file and stays true.

Suppressed is sourced from a wiki article infobox rather than from a module, so it is curated on the items instead of fetched. It is a real published fact, 12 metres of audible range against 100, and it carries no `judgement` field for that reason. Move it into fetch-wiki.mjs when that script learns to read weapon infoboxes.

The weather rules price a hazard as if it were always happening. A planet listing sandstorms has sandstorms sometimes, roughly three minutes at a time, and nothing in the data says how often. The visibility penalties are set as a risk you carry across a run rather than a state you are in, which is a judgement and not a measurement.

Peril is 6 * (difficulty - 5) + SQUAD_PRESSURE[squad], where the squad curve is [10, 4, 1, 0] taken from the wiki patrol interval multipliers. The two zero points are the curator's calibration from play: a four stack is comfortable through 5 and solo through 3. Only three rules read it, all on the bot front, so difficulty and squad still move nothing on bugs or squids.

Three rules scale off peril rather than gating on it as of 1.19.0, so solo at 7 and solo at 10 no longer move the same items by the same amount. All three are on the bot front. Nothing on bugs or squids scales off it, and that is where the gradient is still missing.

The negative half is defined and barely used. peril-bots-punishes-loud hands out a bonus below zero peril and explains it with its sayInverted, and it is the only rule doing anything down there. Nothing yet says that anti tank at difficulty 3 is firepower for an enemy that does not spawn.

A rule scaling off peril must not name a squad size in its say. Peril is 6 * (difficulty - 5) + SQUAD_PRESSURE[squad] and depth reaches it as readily as being alone does, so four players on Super Helldive sit at 30. All three bot peril rules shipped in 1.19.0 asserting the reader was outnumbered, and their inverted halves asserted the reader was not, both on a figure that says neither. Fixed on 22 August 2026 by describing the pressure instead. Nothing about how a squad size might get its own wording is solved here; the rule simply may not claim one it did not check.
